newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea posts record trade deficit for 1996.
newsitem.headline: South Korea posts record trade deficit for 1996.

text.p: South Korea on Friday posted a record annual trade deficit of $20.38 billion for 1996, chiefly the result of plunging prices for computer chips, but economists said the picture should improve later this year.
The government, meanwhile, said the battle against the ballooning deficit would be the top priority this year along with the fight against inflation.
"Our economic policies will focus on reduction of the current account deficit and price stability," Finance and Economy Minister Han Seung-soo said in a statement.

Trade Ministry figures released Friday showed December's customs-cleared deficit soared to $1.37 billion from $49 million a year ago. That helped double the full year shortfall to $20.38 billion from $10.06 billion last year.
Pushed by the trade deficit, South Korea's current account shortfall is officially forecast to hit $22 billion in calendar 1996, compared with an $8.95 billion deficit in 1995.
The current account measures trade in goods and services and certain financial transfers.
The ministry also blamed rising imports of crude oil, the result of a huge expansion by refiners, and a growing taste for luxury imports by South Koreans for the dismal figures.
Officials have declined to forecast this year's trade deficit, but analysts said a slowdown in falling chip prices and a stronger yen should help exporters.
